messages.subject: Shiny data table Vs View()
parts:
It seems that the View() in R-Studio provides more robust filtering capabilities with sliders and check-box selections. I would rather use the View() functionality if it was integrated into shiny to start with. If these functions were available to shiny app with a handle to the filtered output, that enables interactivity with graphs, etc. Basically it become part of the UI functions.

Question-1: from inside shiny: Is it possible to fork a separate window Viewer in R Studio. For example, View(iris) in a new window
Question-2: Related to Question-1, after filtering, can I get a handle to the filtered data of the View() window

Thanks
MJJ

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Shiny data table Vs View()
parts:
1. No.

2. You may use the DT package. Please see the section "Column Filters"
in the documentation: http://rstudio.github.io/DT/ and
http://rstudio.github.io/DT/shiny.html

Regards,
Yihui
